title.narrative: Activity under preparation Global Gateway Transport Support Action

description.narrative: In line with the external dimension of the EU Green Deal, the EU Energy & Climate Diplomacy, the transport sector in its railway and maritime sub-sectors is at a critical juncture with the potential to play a significant role in global decarbonisation efforts. The EU external action on transport has become more strategic and geopolitical, and the relation with and support to EU companies has become a key priority. EU values and its regulatory framework contribution towards rail and maritime global sectors sustainability is key to also to find entry points supporting EU industry competitivity. This action will complement EU¿s support to international organisations such as the International Maritime Organization (IMO) activities involving several countries sharing EU values also looking for further support to EU¿s efforts on the regulatory front. In a similar manner, it will promote through entities such as the European Union Agency for Railways (ERA) the EU¿s rail regulatory framework in the African context.  This action aims at completing INTPA¿s toolbox in preparation to scale up the Global Gateway in the next MFF, and includes two main specific objectives: (i) to support partner countries in improving the investment climate and regulatory frameworks to contribute to unlocking investment, (ii) to promote and transpose to partner countries EU values, standards, knowledge, and best practices on sustainable transport, including just and better working conditions for women building the necessary human resources capacity. Three outcomes are expected: (a) specific support to the rail sector in sub-Saharan Africa, (b) on the maritime sector, cooperation with international organisations such as IMO for port governance and green and digital investments preparation (including single window), specifically in sub-Saharan Africa, and (c) support globally on maritime transport-related gender issues.  The African maritime and port governance components, as well as the project on African rail, are key to the continent's efforts in maritime and rail decarbonisation and promoting greener, safer, and more socially responsible transportation. The actions include capacity building aiming to develop advanced training capacity for a new generation of seafarers proficient in decarbonised and digital shipping operations. Additionally, this action will contribute to combating violence and harassment in the maritime industry, with the goal of fostering a culture of zero tolerance and strengthening regulatory frameworks, in line with EU commitments to promote decent, safe, and fair employment, and improve workplace safety and culture at sea. the EU's perspective, supporting these actions is crucial as it aligns with the EU's own goals of reducing emissions, promoting sustainable transportation, and ensuring safe and fair working conditions, and demonstrates the EU's commitment to cooperation and partnership with African countries in achieving these shared objectives, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable and equitable global maritime industry. The proposed maritime and railway components contribute to the NDICI-Global Europe `Global Challenges¿ Priority area on Prosperity, directly addressing climate change mitigation through GHG emission reduction in international maritime shipping, maritime and port governance, the green transition and promoting zero tolerance
